answer: Proof-of-replication storage binds each agent to its own disk: every identity must hold a unique sealed copy of a large dataset, encoded with its key, and answer random spot-checks fast. A quartz-steady honest node seals once, but N fake heads need N separately sealed copies, so storage cost climbs with every head. When checks hit like a falcon, a farm reusing one copy sinks to its nadir and loses each bond.
